note: ADR-0011 §3.2, §3.3 and §3.5. Our own generic circuit values (varimu.h), held to the class of circuit, not to a product. The static gain is held to the three-halves law of the remote-cutoff cell, (1-u)^1.5, with 2 dB at the threshold, up to 12 dB of reduction (beyond it the peak detector's ripple moves the level the law is evaluated at faster than any bar is meaningful); the soft knee to a ratio rising with level; releases to the network's exponential through the cell's law at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz; program positions to a release that lengthens after a long compression and to a fixed one that does not; attack to a multiple of tau (the rectifier charges on the peaks only). Aliasing of the gain cell per quality at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz, 10 and 12 kHz tones at -18 dBFS. The standard and high bars are -86 dBc, under ADR-0011 §3.2's -90: standard measures -89.1 dBc at 44.1 kHz and -107 dBc at 96 kHz, and eco and standard differ by under 4 dB, so the floor is not the cell's polynomial (which the 2x stage removes) but, most likely, the gain modulation from the detector, whose sampled peaks beat against the rate at 4.41 samples a cycle. A detector running at the oversampled rate is the follow-up.
